git.name: git_get_context
git.description: Start here for any coding or review task: current branch, upstream ahead/behind, remote URL, recent commits, working tree status, diff stat summary, and Jira keys detected in the branch name. Pass includeDiff=true to also include the full uncommitted diff.

repoPath.description: Path to the git repository (defaults to cwd)

commitLimit.description: Number of recent commits to show (default 10)

git.name: git_get_diff
git.description: Get a diff between two git refs or commits. Use when you need to compare a feature branch to main, inspect a specific commit range, or review changes between two refs. For large diffs, increase maxChars or use charOffset to page through them.

repoPath.description: Path to the git repository (defaults to cwd)

maxChars.description: Max characters to return (default 8000). Increase for large diffs.

charOffset.description: Skip this many characters from the start (for paging large diffs)

context.name: get_dev_context
context.description: Master entry point for "what am I working on / what's the status", and before any review or coding task. Returns: git branch + upstream state, Jira ticket overview (status, transitions, sprint, comments), open PR with reviewer approvals, and actionable next-step hints (create PR, merge, address blockers).

repoPath.description: Local path to the git repo (defaults to cwd)

jira.name: start_work
jira.description: Start working on a Jira ticket end-to-end: resolves the ticket (by key or free-text search with a picker when multiple match), creates a local branch with an auto-generated name, fetches the project README from Bitbucket so you have commit/PR conventions in context, and prints a next-steps summary. If issueKey is omitted, provide query for free-text search.

issueKey.description: Jira issue key, e.g. FOO-123 (provide this OR query)

query.description: Free-text search when issueKey is unknown — shows a picker if multiple tickets match

transitionName.description: Jira transition to apply, e.g. "In Progress" (optional)

push.description: Push branch to remote after creation (default false)

jira.name: jira_search
jira.description:
Discover Jira resources (tickets, projects, boards, sprints, versions, users). Set resource:
• "issues" (default) — search by text, JQL, project, status, assignee, issue type, or mine=true for your queue
• "projects" — list all projects and their keys
• "issue_types" — valid types and statuses for a project
• "boards" — list boards (pass project to filter by project key); use this to find the boardId before fetching sprints or board_overview
• "sprints" — sprints for a board (pass boardId); if you don't know the boardId, first use resource=boards
• "board_overview" — active/future sprints with their issues for a board (pass boardId); use when asked "what's in the sprint", "show me the board", or "what's everyone working on"
• "versions" — list fix versions/releases for a project (pass project; optionally pass query to filter by name substring). If the version you need does not exist, create it yourself with `jira_version action=create` — do NOT ask the user to make it in the Jira UI.
• "users" — find users by name/email (pass query)

mine.description: Return issues assigned to you (resource=issues only)

query.description: Text search or user name query

jql.description: Raw JQL (resource=issues only, overrides other filters)

project.description: Project key filter or scope for issue_types/boards

status.description: Status filter (issues only, or board_overview to filter issues by status)

assignee.description: Assignee username filter (issues only, or board_overview to filter issues by assignee)

boardId.description: Board ID (required for resource=sprints or board_overview)

sprintState.description: Sprint state filter: active, future, closed (sprints and board_overview)

includeIssues.description: Include issues per sprint in board_overview (default true)

jira.name: jira_get
jira.description: Full details for one Jira issue: summary, description, status, assignee, sprint, available transitions, recent comments, and a list of attachments (filename, size, mime type, attachment ID). To view an attachment's contents (e.g. an image), call jira_get_attachment with the attachment ID surfaced here.

fullDescription.description: Return the full description even when long (default false — descriptions over ~2000 chars are truncated to save context)

jira.name: jira_mutate
jira.description: Create/update a ticket, transition status, assign, comment, link issues, or log work — bundles create/update/transition/comment/link/worklog in one call. Use Jira wiki markup (Atlassian renderer syntax), not GitHub/CommonMark markdown.

issueKey.description: Existing issue key to mutate (optional if create is provided)

projectKey.description: Jira project code (optional, auto-resolved when omitted)

issueType.description: Issue type name, e.g. Bug, Story, Task, Sub-task

description.description: Issue description (optional). Use Jira wiki markup (Atlassian renderer syntax), not GitHub/CommonMark markdown.

parent.description: Parent issue key. For Sub-task issue types this sets the Jira parent. If the key points to an Epic, the Epic Link custom field is set automatically instead (Jira Server epic membership).

epicLink.description: Epic issue key to attach the new issue to as an epic child (Jira Server Epic Link). Overrides parent if both are passed.

description.description: New description (optional). Use Jira wiki markup (Atlassian renderer syntax), not GitHub/CommonMark markdown.

assignee.description: New assignee username, or empty string to unassign (optional)

fixVersion.description: Fix version name, or empty string to clear (optional)

epicLink.description: Epic issue key to set as parent epic (Jira Server Epic Link), or empty string to clear.

sprintId.description: Sprint ID to add the issue into (optional)

removeFromSprint.description: Move the issue to the backlog (remove from any sprint)

transitionName.description: Transition name, e.g. "In Progress" (optional if transitionId provided)

comment.description: Comment to add after other mutations (optional). Use Jira wiki markup (Atlassian renderer syntax), not GitHub/CommonMark markdown.

link.description: Create an issue link, e.g. "FOO-123 blocks BAR-456"

targetIssueKey.description: The other issue in the relationship

direction.description: outward (default): issueKey → target; inward: target → issueKey

worklog.description: Log time spent on this issue

timeSpent.description: Time in Jira format, e.g. "2h 30m" or "1d"

started.description: ISO 8601 datetime when work started (defaults to now)

jira.name: jira_get_attachment
jira.description: Fetch a Jira attachment by ID and return its contents inline. Images are auto-resized + re-encoded; text/JSON/XML return as text; videos and animated images (GIF/APNG/animated WebP) are decoded with ffmpeg into sampled frames (re-call with start/end/frames or mode=scenes to refine); audio returns as an audio block; PDFs return extracted text. Oversized/non-renderable files are saved to a temp file and the path returned. Use jira_get first to discover attachment IDs.

attachmentId.description: Numeric attachment ID from jira_get output

saveTo.description: Optional absolute path to save the original (un-resized) file to disk instead of returning inline

maxDimension.description: Max long-edge size in pixels for inline images (default 1568 for images, 768 for video frames).

quality.description: JPEG quality for re-encoded inline images (1-100, default 85 for images, 65 for video frames). Ignored for images with alpha (encoded as PNG).

frames.description: Video/animated-image only: number of frames to sample (default 6, range 1-60). Higher = more detail + more context.

start.description: Video/animated-image only: start of sample window in seconds (default 0). Use with end/frames to zoom into a moment of interest after a coarse first pass.

end.description: Video/animated-image only: end of sample window in seconds (default full duration). Must be greater than start.

mode.description: Video/animated-image only: "uniform" samples N frames evenly (default); "scenes" uses ffmpeg scene-change detection, better for screencasts/narrative content.

sceneThreshold.description: Video/animated-image only: scene-change sensitivity in 0-1 (default 0.3). Only used when mode=scenes. Lower = more frames, higher = fewer.

jira.name: jira_comment
jira.description: Add, update, or delete a comment on a Jira issue. action defaults to "add". Can only edit/delete your own comments. Use Jira wiki markup (Atlassian renderer syntax), not GitHub/CommonMark markdown.

body.description: Comment text. Use Jira wiki markup (Atlassian renderer syntax), not GitHub/CommonMark markdown. Required for add/update.

jira.name: jira_version
jira.description: Manage Jira fix versions (releases): create, update, release, archive, delete. action defaults to "create". For create pass projectKey + name. For update/release/archive/delete pass id (look it up via jira_search resource=versions). "release" sets released=true and defaults releaseDate to today. Once a version exists you can set it on tickets via jira_mutate update.fixVersion.

projectKey.description: Jira project code (required for create when not auto-resolvable)

id.description: Version id (required for update/release/archive/delete; look up via jira_search resource=versions)

name.description: Version name, e.g. "9.1.0" (required for create; optional rename for update)

releaseDate.description: Release date in YYYY-MM-DD (optional; defaults to today on action=release)

bitbucket.name: bitbucket_search
bitbucket.description:
Discover Bitbucket resources (PRs, repos, branches, users). Set resource:
• "pull_requests" (default) — list PRs by state/branch/text; mine=true for your inbox
• "repos" — list repositories in a project
• "branches" — list or filter branches in a repo
• "users" — find users by name/email (pass query); add projectKey+repoSlug to restrict to users with repo access. ALWAYS use this to look up valid usernames before adding reviewers to a PR.

mine.description: Return your own PRs by role (resource=pull_requests only)

repoPath.description: Local path of the repo to auto-detect project/repo from (overrides workspace roots). Usually unnecessary if projectKey+repoSlug are given.

fromBranch.description: Filter PRs from this source branch

bitbucket.name: bitbucket_get_pr
bitbucket.description: Full details for one PR: metadata, commits, open comments, blockers, optional diff, and any attachments referenced from the description or comments (with attachment ID + filename). IMPORTANT: The PR branch is often not the locally checked-out branch. Do NOT read files with local tools (Read, git_get_diff, etc.) for PR context — use bitbucket_get_file with the PR's source branch instead. To view an attachment's contents, call bitbucket_get_attachment with the surfaced attachment ID. The response includes a "Viewing as" line — if it says "you are the author", do NOT add review comments or a summary unless explicitly asked; just answer questions about the PR. If it says "you are a reviewer", default to posting inline comments for suggested changes and a final summary comment.

repoPath.description: Local path of the repo to auto-detect project/repo from (overrides workspace roots). Usually unnecessary if projectKey+repoSlug are given.

prId.description: Pull request number (optional if fromBranch provided or running from a checked-out branch)

fromBranch.description: Source branch — auto-resolves the open PR; omit to use current checked-out branch

includeComments.description: Include review comments and blockers (default true)

includeBuildStatus.description: Include CI/build status for the head commit (default true)

commentsState.description: Comment state filter (default ALL — returns every comment with its state badge so nothing is silently hidden). Pass OPEN/RESOLVED only when explicitly narrowing.

fullDescription.description: Return the full PR description even when long (default false — descriptions over ~2000 chars are truncated to save context)

bitbucket.name: bitbucket_mutate
bitbucket.description: Create, update, approve/unapprove, mark needs_work, decline, or merge a PR — in one call. Auto-targets the open PR for the current branch when prId is omitted. needs_work sets your reviewer status to "Needs work" (Bitbucket Server's changes-requested signal); revert with action=unapprove.

repoPath.description: Local path of the repo to auto-detect project/repo from (overrides workspace roots). Usually unnecessary if projectKey+repoSlug are given.

prId.description: Target PR number (optional, auto-resolved from branch)

action.description: Lifecycle action to perform (optional). needs_work = mark your reviewer status as "Needs work" (changes requested).

reviewers.description: Reviewer usernames. Use bitbucket_search resource=users to look up valid usernames before setting this.

pickReviewers.description: Show an interactive reviewer picker before creating the PR (lists users with repo access)

description.description: Updated description, or empty string to clear (optional)

reviewers.description: Updated reviewer usernames. Empty array clears reviewers. Use bitbucket_search resource=users to look up valid usernames before setting this.

bitbucket.name: bitbucket_comment
bitbucket.description: Add, update, or delete a PR comment. action defaults to "add". This tool posts COMMENTS, never tasks — never set severity=BLOCKER to create a task. severity=BLOCKER is rejected on add and only ever valid on update to escalate an already-blocking comment. To create a task, use bitbucket_pr_tasks (action=create), and only when the user explicitly asks for a task. For code changes, ALWAYS use inline comments with suggestion when exact replacement code is available. Keep any explanatory text before the suggestion block only (never after), or Bitbucket may hide Apply suggestion. Replies MUST use commentId. Only one reply per thread per author: if you already replied to a comment, update your existing reply (action=update commentId=<your-reply-id>) instead of posting a second one. The server enforces this and will reject the second add. Keep comments concise, no emojis. Only call proactively (without being asked) when you are a reviewer on the PR (i.e. "Viewing as" says "you are a reviewer") — never post unsolicited comments on PRs you authored. For inline comments: ALWAYS pass fromHash + toHash matching the commit you actually reviewed (read from bitbucket_pr_diff or bitbucket_get_pr output). Without them the anchor falls back to current PR head, and if the branch advanced between review and post the line number will point at unrelated code. When the comment body references another comment by id, render it as a markdown hyperlink `[#<id>](<baseUrl>/projects/<PROJECT>/repos/<REPO>/pull-requests/<prId>/overview?commentId=<id>)` — never a bare `#<id>`, which is unclickable in Bitbucket's renderer.

repoPath.description: Local path of the repo to auto-detect project/repo from (overrides workspace roots). Usually unnecessary if projectKey+repoSlug are given.

commentId.description: Comment ID to reply to, update, or delete

text.description: Comment text for add/update. No filler, no emojis. If suggestion is used, keep this optional and brief; it is placed before the suggestion block.

filePath.description: File path for inline comment (must pair with line)

srcPath.description: Source path if file was renamed (optional, defaults to filePath)

line.description: Line number to anchor inline comment (must pair with filePath)

fileType.description: Diff side: TO (new, default) or FROM (old)

multilineStartLine.description: First line of multiline anchor (pair with line as last line)

fromHash.description: Base/target commit of the diff you reviewed (from bitbucket_pr_diff or bitbucket_get_pr). Pair with toHash so the anchor binds to the exact commit, not whatever the PR head happens to be at post time.

toHash.description: Source/feature commit of the diff you reviewed (from bitbucket_pr_diff or bitbucket_get_pr). Pair with fromHash. If the PR has advanced since, Bitbucket will mark the comment outdated — that is the correct behaviour.

suggestion.description: Replacement code to suggest. Use whenever proposing a concrete code change. Posted as the final ```suggestion``` block so Apply suggestion appears. Requires filePath + line.

state.description: Task state for BLOCKER comments (update only)

severity.description: Comment severity. Leave unset — comments default to NORMAL. BLOCKER turns the comment into a task and is REJECTED on add; only pass BLOCKER on update to escalate an existing comment when the user explicitly asks. To create a task, use bitbucket_pr_tasks instead.

bitbucket.name: bitbucket_get_file
bitbucket.description: Raw file content from Bitbucket at a branch, tag, or commit. CRITICAL: if the PR branch being reviewed is NOT the currently checked-out local branch, ALL additional file context for that review MUST come from this tool — never from local Read, git_get_diff, or any tool that reads local disk. Pass the PR source branch as ref.

repoPath.description: Local path of the repo to auto-detect project/repo from (overrides workspace roots). Usually unnecessary if projectKey+repoSlug are given.

ref.description: Branch, tag, or commit hash (defaults to default branch)

bitbucket.name: bitbucket_get_attachment
bitbucket.description: Fetch a Bitbucket repo attachment by ID and return its contents inline. Attachments are repo-scoped, referenced from PR descriptions/comments via attachment:<id> markdown; use bitbucket_get_pr first to surface IDs. Images are auto-resized + re-encoded; text/JSON/XML return as text; videos and animated images (GIF/APNG/animated WebP) are decoded with ffmpeg into sampled frames (re-call with start/end/frames or mode=scenes to refine); audio returns as an audio block; PDFs return extracted text. Oversized/non-renderable files are saved to a temp file and the path returned.

repoPath.description: Local path of the repo to auto-detect project/repo from (overrides workspace roots). Usually unnecessary if projectKey+repoSlug are given.

saveTo.description: Optional absolute path to save the original (un-resized) file to disk instead of returning inline

maxDimension.description: Max long-edge size in pixels for inline images (default 1568 for images, 768 for video frames).

quality.description: JPEG quality for re-encoded inline images (1-100, default 85 for images, 65 for video frames). Ignored for images with alpha (encoded as PNG).

frames.description: Video/animated-image only: number of frames to sample (default 6, range 1-60).

start.description: Video/animated-image only: start of sample window in seconds (default 0). Use with end/frames to zoom in.

end.description: Video/animated-image only: end of sample window in seconds (default full duration). Must be greater than start.

mode.description: Video/animated-image only: "uniform" samples N frames evenly (default); "scenes" uses scene-change detection.

sceneThreshold.description: Video/animated-image only: scene-change sensitivity in 0-1 (default 0.3). Only used when mode=scenes. Lower = more frames, higher = fewer.

bitbucket.name: bitbucket_pr_tasks
bitbucket.description: Manage PR tasks (checklist items): list, create, resolve, reopen, delete. Tasks are distinct from comments — they appear as a checklist in the PR sidebar.

repoPath.description: Local path of the repo to auto-detect project/repo from (overrides workspace roots). Usually unnecessary if projectKey+repoSlug are given.

commentId.description: Anchor the task to a specific comment ID (optional for create)

combined.name: complete_work
combined.description: Close the loop on a finished branch: merges the open PR and transitions the Jira ticket to Done (or a named transition). Mirrors start_work.

issueKey.description: Jira issue key to transition (auto-detected from branch name if omitted)

prId.description: PR to merge (auto-detected from current branch if omitted)

transitionName.description: Jira transition to apply after merge (default: "Done")

skipJiraTransition.description: Skip transitioning the Jira ticket (default false)
